title: spring-framework@db9a10bf: simpleMatch's prefix check as startsWith (positive scaffold)
summary: Framework's 2021 change of one expression in `PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch(String,String)`, from `pattern.substring(0, i).equals(str.substring(0, i))` to `pattern.startsWith(str.substring(0, i))`. The positive of the binder decision-string family: both revisions should return the same boolean and exceptions over a bounded UTF-16 domain. Maven Central's spring-core 5.3.6 and 5.3.7 carry exactly the parent's and child's source. A scaffold: source-locked, tasks named, not yet run.
notes: A positive scaffold of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md (positive stream): an expected outcome for named claims on one upstream change, never a statement that the release is secure. Readiness and proof outcomes come from receipts, not from this file.

Source lock checked upstream on 2026-11-14 (sources.lock.json): db9a10bf's only parent is 27bfcbbc. PatternMatchUtils.java at 27bfcbbc and v5.3.6, and in spring-core-5.3.6-sources.jar, is one blob (04301284); at db9a10bf and v5.3.7, and in spring-core-5.3.7-sources.jar, another (67871015). So the release pair 5.3.6 -> 5.3.7 runs the commits' original method bytecode from Maven Central, with no upstream build.
simpleMatch(String,String) calls only String methods and itself, and the class has no static initializer.

The native checker of application-core takes a String parameter as bounded UTF-16 with content and never null, and refuses null: the claim's null pattern and string are part of the declared domain, so a refusal there is reported, not dropped.

The packet (2026-11-14): claims/simple-match-preservation.json (each String null or at most 6 UTF-16 code units of any value, maxArrayLength 6, unwind 16); replay/probes.json (40 probes: the brief's nine, empty and no-star patterns, leading, internal, trailing and repeated stars, a prefix mismatch, non-ASCII, a surrogate pair, half a pair and isolated surrogates); controls/oracle.py (a dynamic-programming glob decision over code units, unlike either revision's search and recursion); replay/driver (one JSON line per probe, arguments as hex code units so surrogates arrive exactly); controls/drop-prefix.patch (the mutant, on release-after).

A hand replay on 2026-11-14, a note and not evidence: the driver compiled with javac 25.0.5 --release 21 (driver.jar sha256 bd9de983...) and run with the sidecar's pinned JARs on Temurin 21.0.13 and 25.0.5. Both releases agree with the oracle on all 40 probes and with each other, identically on both JDKs (22 true, 18 false). The mutant (the patched class compiled --release 8 into a copy of spring-core-5.3.7.jar, sha256 c0489de1...) disagrees on 6: abc* against xbcdef and abd, é* against ex and Éx, ABC* against abcdef, and \ud800* against \udc00x, all true where the statement says false.

A static jvmcontract gaps scan (records/simple-match-gaps.json, a note, with a binary one lib/src commit old) lists seven JDK String methods both revisions reach that the native checker approximates (substring, endsWith and indexOf), so the strict preservation attempt is predicted to be refused by name; the null cases are a second predicted refusal. Both are predicted blockers in target.json, not observations.

Mutation control as a revision (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5): controls/drop-prefix.patch is declared in target.json as workflow W1's constructed revision `mutant` (base `release-after`, the patch's sha256 locked), the after of the `mutation` pair. It has two tasks of its own: `mutant-replay`, the concrete controls on that pair, where the base must hold and the mutant fail the oracle, and `mutant-preservation`, preservation's claim on the mutant, expected refuted. Its claim is bound to the mutant's artifact (runtime's identity `mutant:<base commit>+<patch sha256>`), never to a release's. It used to be only a `controls` entry on `release-after`, which no task prepared.

Companions and tags (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5): target.json's identity names 286, this family's CVE packet, as its companion, as 286 names this one; the example is tagged external-target, as every example with a sidecar is, and data-binding, its family's domain tag. It was tagged request-binding, a defect tag for a handler parameter that can't bind, which PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch is not; data-binding is the domain of DataBinder's field checks, which call it.

Runner interface (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5 step 1, request 9): controls/oracle.py also defines driver_args(), the driver's whole argument vector (the same as `oracle.py argv`), and problems(lines), one revision's driver lines in, [(probe, problem)] out, where the independent statement disagrees; an exception is a replay that can't be judged, never a violation. runtime.run_controls passes driver_args() and keeps every line the driver prints, its preparation copies the probes file with the oracle, and workflow_ingest reads each revision with problems() against what its pair's kind expects (examples/tools/targets/runtime.py's docstring). Before this, the merged runner looked for a PROBES list and ingestion called check(lines), so the controls could not have run. The CLI (`argv`, `check`, the pair comparison) is unchanged.
